note: Both sets cover the same core facts (dishwasher temperatures, sensor count, capacity, heated-drying disablement, and the clothes-drying scoring thresholds) and both repeat several facts under two names. Set A states the 115°F half-points condition correctly, including that the sensor must not reach 120°F, and its quotes match the page. Set B misquotes the wash/rinse requirement ('at least one wash and rinse and cycle') and drops the 'does not reach 120°F' condition from one of its 115°F claims, while adding an extra duplicate of the heated-drying claim.
remarks: Both sets heavily duplicate facts (sensor count, 120°F, 115°F, and each scoring threshold appear twice under different entity/attribute names), inflating claim counts without adding information. Both also omit notable page facts: the temperature-of-record rule (higher of two sensor readings, or lower if the higher sensor is defective), the definition of cycle 'interruption', cycle-completion confirmation by audible/visible signal, permitted load states (empty/partial/fully loaded, soiled or clean), the two-loads-per-day requirement with separate scoring, and the demonstration requirement for visible drying methods.
